sophia: bringing up mistral-9b int8 on dedicated pool, seeing embedding drift vs our llama baseline :eyes:

dinesh: what sort of drift? cosine sim numbers? any conversion steps you ran?

sophia: quick numbers: avg cos sim on eval set = 0.78 vs 0.96 for fp16 hosted-llama. conversion pipeline: hf -> internal-convert v2 -> quantize int8 (per-channel). suspect rotary/headscale or vocab remap.

marco: have you checked tokenizer id maps? sometimes mistral exports have extra sentinels/merged tokens that shift ids during our conversion.

sophia: good call — found a sample: `"Hello, world!"` maps to id 345 on llama, 357 on mistral-export after conversion. tokenizer config had `preprocess: nfkc` earlier.

kai: two quick hypotheses: 1) token id aliasing (vocab grafting) 2) rotary head-scale mismatch after int8 proj reorder. try forcing token remap and a tiny rotary rescale patch `ROTARY_SCALE=1.0003` to test.

marco: also try running quantize with symmetric calibration instead of per-channel — we saw headwise scale sensitivity on orpheus conversion.

infra-bot: deployment: dedicated/gpu-pool-3 restarted (1729943230) for new model image roll. :gear:

sophia: ran token remap + rotary rescale + symmetric calibration quick test. results: cos sim -> 0.94, generation fidelity on short prompts looks fine, but longctx perplexity up ~6% on 8k windows.

dinesh: interesting — improved local align but long context degrade suggests kv-cache alignment or rotary phase wrap differing under int8. did you check kvcache warmup behavior?

sophia: seeing small logits drift after 64 tokens warmup. dump shows phase angles slightly off per-head.

kai: can you paste the small repro snippet? also try disabling headwise quantization fallback (set QUANT_FALLBACK=off) to see if per-head scaling inconsistency is caused by fallback heuristics.

sophia: repro snippet:

```
# run on dedicated pool image
python serve_eval.py --model /models/mistral-9b-int8-conv \
  --eval longctx_qa --batch 1 --max_len 4096 --log_angles
```

marco: once you have logs, run the headscale audit tool: `tools/headscale-audit --model ... --compare /models/llama-7b-fp16`. it graphs headwise rotary norm diffs.

sophia: ran headscale-audit: most heads within 0.2% but head 11 and 23 show 3-5% phase magnitude diff. after forcing rotary rescale on those heads only, longctx perplexity dropped back near baseline.

dinesh: that tracks — probably conversion reorders proj weights causing tiny FP rounding changes that amplify under int8. mitigation: per-head rotary rescale table in conversion step + token id alias map during conversion. want me to PR the conversion patch?

sophia: yes please. also will run full eval harness overnight (incl. multilingual/commonsense) and post numbers tomorrow. thanks y'all :thumbsup:

kai: nice triage. add an integration test to ensure token ids roundtrip (sample 10k tokens) and headscale max-deviation < 1% post-quantization.

infra-bot: scheduled: nightly-evals job started for mistral-9b-int8-conv (1729943270)

sophia: noted — will follow up with eval artifacts + diff plots in the morning.
